name: MANGAL · the Tuesday gold season
one_line: One word, MANGAL, which means auspicious and in most Indian languages also names Tuesday, titles Naira's season from Karwa Chauth to the first muhurats; every tile is a drawn object from Mummy's house with a real, photographed Naira piece inside it, told as a numbered House Rule under one NAIRA + MANGAL seal whose script changes post by post, and the spine is the owner's own line: Not locker gold. Tuesday gold.
big_idea: In Marathi, Hindi, Gujarati, Bengali, Kannada, Telugu, Punjabi and Urdu, Tuesday is named for Mangal, and mangal also means auspicious. The festive season is when every Indian house waits for an auspicious day and takes the good gold out of the locker. Naira's answer is the owner's 10/10 line, 'Not locker gold. Tuesday gold.': jewellery for the ordinary days in between, which in eight languages are already called mangal. So the season gets one title, written the way PTAT wrote MILNI. P1 sets MANGAL in four words with the Ruby Baguette Tennis Bracelet on the cover; slide 2 is the dictionary page with the full verified table. After that, every object tile carries one compact seal in the same bottom band (the kit NAIRA wordmark, MANGAL, and ONE script word under it, a different language each post, gated by a native reader), and every caption ends 'Today's mangal: <language>, <word>.' Under the title runs HOUSE RULES N° 01 to 10, the rules every Indian mother enforced (moon first; the good gold lives in the locker; ek aur; the dabba never goes back empty; shagun ends in one; one ring means I've reached; name on everything; the good box is never thrown away; shubh mangal saavdhan), each staged on the object itself, drawn, with the real piece as the punchline. One honesty rule is also the look: everything drawn is from Mummy's house, everything photographed is for sale. Every Tuesday post lands in column 3, so the right-hand column of the finished grid is the season's four Mangalvaars, and the long diagonal runs from MANGAL (P1, bottom-right) to SHUBH MANGAL. SAAVDHAN. (P12, top-left), where the season's ruby set closes as one BUY3 basket.
why_it_wins: It is the option that looks most like the reference the owner shared and is built entirely from her own material. PTAT's system, translated not copied: a multi-script season title (MILNI to MANGAL), one lockup bracketed by two motifs (marigolds and a mehndi hand become the bag's coral tulips and Mummy's almirah key), real photographs inside drawn frames (the almirah mirror), a steel serving surface as the guide (the thali, with a menu card), series with volumes (House Rule N°, The Mangal Thali vol 1). The reference judge scored it highest of all four (87). It carries most of the owner's top-scored caption-doc lines: 'Not locker gold. Tuesday gold.' (10/10), the dabba (9.5), the missed call (9.5), the good box. And it runs on the account's winning ad formula, one everyday Indian object, one real piece, one witty Indian line, the formula of 'Anaar, pre-peeled.' (₹335 per purchase, ROAS 4.52). The fixes in this brief answer every judge: the P1 cover now sells the Ruby bracelet on blush with no sunburst or garlands; there is one brand band per tile, with no top-left wordmark stacked on top of the seal; prices come off covers; there are no orange grounds and the plum is lifted so it never reads black; the owner's two approved plates (P5, P11) stay clean; the densest guide (the Shaadi Calendar) is cut; the two hardest drawings are simplified (the locker list; the antarpat without hands); the BUY line is in 7 captions; COD and insured shipping are in four first comments and a reel end card; every Indic word is gated by a named native reader, with a Marathi fallback. It asks for zero AI generations. Of the 36 frames, all jewellery is real listing photography or BiRefNet cut-outs of it.

posts.concept: Every Indian house has the rule: the good gold lives in the locker of the steel almirah and comes out for weddings. The owner's own 10/10 line is the headline, with the tone bracket in the same frame. Slide 2 opens only the locker door: Mummy's handwritten LOCKER LIST is taped inside it, and the real hoops hang outside on a hook. Slide 3 gives the facts.

posts.concept: At a Marathi wedding the antarpat, the cloth held between the couple, drops on one word, 'saavdhan', the refrain of the mangalashtak 'shubh mangal saavdhan', and every guest looks up at once. The finale draws that cloth, oxblood silk with a gold zari border, hanging taut from a gold cord on two clips, with SHUBH MANGAL. SAAVDHAN. as the season's biggest lockup between the tulips and the chaabi. In the reel the cord lets go, the cloth drops through yellow akshata and reveals the ruby baguette necklace at the base of a neck; then the season's three ruby pieces come together as one set. It bookends P1 on the diagonal: the season began with MANGAL and ends with SHUBH MANGAL.

posts.alt_text: Cover of a short video on a deep plum ground: a dark red silk cloth with a gold zari border hangs from a gold cord on two brass clips, coral tulips at one corner and a steel key with a blush tassel hanging from the other. On the cloth in cream and gold: Shubh Mangal. Saavdhan. and the same words in Marathi script. In the video yellow rice falls, the cord lets go, the cloth drops and reveals a ruby-red baguette necklace worn at the base of the neck, then the ruby bracelet, huggies and necklace appear together with their prices: 1,699, 1,199 and 2,300 rupees.
posts.why: From 22 Nov the top-left tile is the first thing every ad visitor sees, so it carries the season's largest lockup, the hero stone and the season's closing basket: the three ruby pieces the option sold one by one (bracelet P1, huggies P6, necklace here) come together as one BUY3 set (graft G3, from Matching Centre). The Baguette Tennis Necklace has 70 in stock and 0 sales; ruby is the hero stone. 'Shubh mangal saavdhan' is the most culturally exact Marathi wedding moment in any proposal (brand judge) for a base that is 46% Maharashtra. Fixes: no drawn hands (a cord and two clips), plum lifted, a ruby-set end card with list prices and no total.
